scalesUsed.notes: B - D - E - F - F# - A

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Tour-de-force 7/4 time signature progressive blues rock that unexpectedly shifts into straight 4/4 for one of the greatest guitar solos of all time
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: D major is the relative major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: 12-bar minor blues progression played in an asymmetric 7/4 time signature, shifting to 4/4 for the solo.
mainProgression.description: 12-bar minor blues progression played in an asymmetric 7/4 time signature, shifting to 4/4 for the solo.

sectionProgressions.progression: Bm (2 bars) - Em (1 bar) - Bm (1 bar) - F#m/Em (1 bar)
sectionProgressions.description: The iconic 7-beat walking bass riff accompanied by rhythmic coin jingles and cash register clicks
Tight staccato chord stabs on beats 1, 3, 5, and 7 supporting the cynical vocal lyrics

sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - iv - i - v - iv - i
sectionProgressions.description: David Gilmour's three-part solo (dry Strat → double-tracked fuzz → soaring wet delay) shifting into straight 4/4 rock

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Heavy, swaggering minor tonic anchored by the 7/4 bassline
Em (iv) - Minor subdominant raising the tension in the 12-bar blues cycle
F#m (v) - Minor dominant providing dark, brooding turnaround resolution

techniques.name: 7/4 Asymmetric Meter & Three-Stage Solo Dynamics
techniques.description: Internalizing the 7/4 time signature (counted as 1-2-3-4-1-2-3) while locking tight with cash register sound effects, followed by a sudden shift to straight 4/4 for epic blues-rock soloing

notes: Bass/guitar riff in 7/4: Fret 2 A (B) → fret 4 A (C#) → fret 4 D (F#) → fret 2 D (E) → fret 4 D (F#) → fret 2 A (B) → fret 2 low E (F#)
Count: 1-2-3-4 (four quarter notes) followed by 1-2-3 (three quarter notes)
Solo shifts to standard 4/4 swing feel at 120 BPM in 7th position B minor pentatonic
sequence: Lock into the 7-beat tape loop of coins and cash registers
Play the walking bass riff with clean, percussive finger or pick attack
Execute the 7/4 staccato chord stabs on Bm7
Switch seamlessly to straight 4/4 when the guitar solo explodes
tips: Gilmour structured the solo in three distinct sonic textures: dry and compressed, double-tracked through a custom fuzz, and wide open with rich reverb/delay
The shift from 7/4 to 4/4 creates an immense feeling of acceleration and release
Count 7/4 as two groups: a measure of 4/4 plus a measure of 3/4

sections.name: 7/4 Main Bass & Guitar Riff
sections.description: One of the most famous odd-meter guitar and bass riffs in music history.
notes: Crisp pick articulation on the single notes
Lock tightly with the rhythmic cash register sound effects

sections.name: 7/4 Verse Chord Stabs
sections.description: Tight staccato chord stabs on Bm7 supporting David Gilmour's vocal lines.
notes: Kill note duration instantly with fretting fingers
Leave space for the vocal narrative

sections.name: 4/4 Guitar Solo Fire
sections.description: Gilmour's legendary three-stage guitar solo shifting into driving 4/4 blues-rock.
notes: Aggressive blues pentatonic bends in 7th position
Screaming pick harmonics and singing vibrato

guitar.pickup: Bridge single-coil for cutting 7/4 riff and searing 4/4 solo lead

amp.recommended: Hiwatt Custom 100 DR103 through WEM 4x12 and Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Colorsound Power Boost & Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (Silicon)
effects.delay: Binson Echorec 2 tape echo (for third solo section)

beginner.title: The 7/4 Riff Notes
steps: Learn the exact note sequence of the walking riff on strings 5, 4, and 6
Lock the riff into continuous loops without hesitating on beat 1

intermediate.title: 7/4 Chords & 4/4 Solo Shift
steps: Master the staccato Bm7 chord stabs in 7/4 time
Practice the metric transition from 7/4 verse into straight 4/4 rock
Play along with the studio track at 120 BPM

advanced.title: The Complete Three-Stage Solo
steps: Learn all three choruses of Gilmour's 4/4 solo note-for-note
Replicate the sonic progression: dry compressed clean → double-tracked fuzz → soaring wet delay
Master Gilmour's aggressive full-step bends, pinch harmonics, and wide vibrato

commonMistakes: Dropping the 7th beat in the 7/4 riff (turning it accidentally into 6/4 or 4/4)
Getting thrown by the sudden time signature shift from 7/4 to 4/4 at the solo
Under-bending on the 10th fret high E string in the solo
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: 7/4 walking riff at 90 BPM → 120 BPM with metronome
5 minutes: Metric transition drill (4 bars of 7/4 into 4 bars of 4/4)
5 minutes: 4/4 solo phrasing and bending practice
focusAreas: Clean staccato muting on chord stabs
Pitch precision on high blues bends
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 7/4 at 100 BPM, counting 1-2-3-4-5-6-7 with accents on beats 1 and 5
